Count definition: a SECURITY node is one with node_kind SECURITY in a partition's nodes list. cash_subclass_nodes = sub_asset_class trimmed and lower-cased equal to cash; already_cash = those whose served asset_class is cash (the builder's value, holdings_snapshot.py line 851 ASSET_CLASS_VALUES); would_move = cash_subclass_nodes minus already_cash. Counted in memory by a read-only script in C:/dev/_scratch373 (outside the worktree); no node value was written to disk.

Upper bound, not a measure of the rule: the proposed rule acts only on the canonical branch (holdings_snapshot.py 977-984, basis TABLE). The served basis TABLE is also written by the fallback when the ticker is in the bd-securities table (_classifier_basis, lines 931-932), so the snapshot does not separate canonical from fallback movers. would_move is therefore an UPPER bound of what the canonical-only rule would move. Movers with basis NAME_ALIAS are fallback answers the rule does not change: cottonwood 215, inflection 67, 49financial 0.

Money-market ticker with no canonical row (code read, not run): bd_securities_fallback.py lines 54-55 (_RE_CASH) and 152-153 return fixed_income for money-market, sweep and cash-reserve names; holdings_snapshot.py 985-994 carries that answer. The proposed rule does not change this layer.
